title: Puffery vs Factual Claims — F2-SUPERLATIVE-SUBSTANTIATED
quote: Measurable claim 'largest' with no visible substantiation/source.
recommendation: Cite the source/basis for the ranking claim, or change to non-factual puffery.

title: Sale / Savings Substantiation — F5-SALE-HAS-DATES
quote: 'Sale' language with no start/end date (perpetual-sale risk).
recommendation: Add genuine start/end dates to sale/savings claims; perpetual sales imply no real prior price.

title: CCPA/CPRA Privacy — PRIV-006
quote: Only 1 request method(s) found: web form
recommendation: Provide at least two methods for consumer privacy requests (e.g., toll-free phone plus email or web form).

title: CCPA/CPRA Privacy — PRIV-008

recommendation: Disclose whether and how the business honors Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signals.

title: CARS Act Total-Payable Disclosure — CA-CARS-003
quote: Monthly payment advertised on vdp_2 without the total amount payable over the term.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, SB 766) | CALIFORNIA controls: CARS Act (SB 766, Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq.), operative Oct 1, 2026. The federal FTC CARS Rule (16 CFR Part 463) was VACATED by the 5th Circuit (Jan 2025) and formally WITHDRAWN from the CFR (Fed. Reg. Feb 2026) — not enforceable. Subsection pin-cites verified against the chaptered statute (leginfo) 2026-06-28.
recommendation: California's CARS-style requirement is not operative until Oct 1, 2026 — fix now to be ready. This is a CALIFORNIA requirement, not a federal one. Under the CARS Act (operative Oct 1, 2026) any monthly-payment ad must also disclose the total the consumer will have paid after all scheduled payments.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh) — ADA-ALT-TEXT
quote: 7 of 22 homepage images missing alt text.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.1.1
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The automated audit could not fully verify this finding (e.g., due to popups, collapsed content, or visual layout). Please visually double-check this item. Add descriptive alt text to images. Missing alt text is the most commonly cited issue in serial ADA/Unruh dealer-website suits.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh) — ADA-FORM-LABELS
quote: 3 of 4 form fields have no associated label/aria-label.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.3.1/4.1.2

Give every input a programmatic label (<label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby). Unlabeled lead-form fields are a frequent ADA/Unruh claim.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh) — ADA-LANG-SKIPNAV
quote: Homepage structure gaps: no skip-to-content link (WCAG 2.4.1).
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1

title: CCPA/CPRA Privacy — PRIV-005 (no substantive written policy on page)
quote: Privacy Policy page renders only site navigation and the ComplyAuto 'Your California Privacy Choices' cookie widget; missing sections: right to know, right to delete, right to correct, sources of PI, retention periods, GPC honoring statement.
recommendation: Publish a complete written CCPA/CPRA privacy policy on /privacy-policy: enumerate all six consumer rights (know, delete, correct, opt-out of sale/share, limit use of sensitive PI, non-discrimination), categories of PI collected, sources, business/commercial purposes, categories of third parties, retention periods, and a statement of how the business honors Global Privacy Control. Data-quality fix: the ComplyAuto opt-out widget covers cookie choices only — do not let it substitute for the full policy text; confirm the policy is server-rendered (not JS-only) so it is crawlable and provable in an exam.

title: Used/CPO discount claims cite a 'List Price' reference with no substantiation or dates
quote: List Price $47,265 Dealer Discount -$10,780 Doc Fee +$85 EVR Filing Fee +$37 Selling Price $36,607
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Automated crawl cannot confirm whether each 'List Price' is a genuine, bona fide former selling price or a synthetic anchor, and the crawl may miss a substantiation note behind a 'Disclosure' expander. Under B&P § 17501 a 'Dealer Discount' from a reference price implies a real prior price. This List Price/Dealer Discount pattern appears site-wide on the used inventory (VLP), CPO page, and used VDPs (e.g., vdp_3, vdp_4) with no visible effective dates. Fix: confirm every advertised 'List Price' maps to a documented, genuine prior price and retain proof; add a short substantiation disclaimer defining 'List Price' and the discount period. Data-quality fix: have the DMS/feed stamp each discount with a start date and the source of the reference price so future audits can verify the anchor automatically.

title: Used vehicle pages do not reference the CARS Act 3-day cancellation right (forward-looking)
quote: 2024 BMW X3 sDrive30i ... Selling Price $29,007 ... 2023 BMW i4 eDrive35 Gran Coupe ... Selling Price $30,707
statute: CARS Act (SB 766; Cal. Civ. Code § 1784.20 et seq.), effective 2026-10-01
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: This is an absence-based, forward-looking finding; the crawl captured only part of each page and a reference may exist in an expander, FAQ, or point-of-sale document. Many used units here are priced at or under $50,000 (e.g., $29,007, $30,707, $27,907, $33,007), so the CARS Act 3-day cancellation right will apply once the statute is operative. No 'all sales final' or 'as-is' waiver language was found in the crawled text (good). Fix now to be ready before the Oct 1, 2026 effective date: add an accurate reference to the 3-day cancellation right on used VLP/VDP pages (3 calendar days, $50,000-or-less threshold, restocking-fee and mileage limits), and confirm no terms/policy pages contradict or waive it. Data-quality fix: template the cancellation-right blurb into the used VDP layout so it renders automatically on every eligible unit rather than being added ad hoc.

title: Lease payment prominent; full Reg M terms sit behind a 'Disclosure' expander
quote: Lease for $431 Per Month For 39 months Plus tax and license. $4877 Due At Signing ... Disclosure
statute: Cal. Veh. Code § 11713.16; Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17500; 12 C.F.R. Part 1013 (Reg M)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Prominence and font-size judgments cannot be made from extracted text. The required content is actually present and complete: each offer shows the monthly payment and due-at-signing inline, and a per-VIN 'Disclosure' expander carries full Reg M terms (MSRP, $0 security deposit, due-at-signing itemization, total of payments, $0.25/mile over 7,500/yr, residual, 09/30/2026 expiration), so this is a best-practice prominence note, not a missing-disclosure violation. Fix: verify the 'Disclosure' link is clearly visible and the itemized due-at-signing has reasonable prominence relative to the large monthly-payment figure on both desktop and mobile; consider surfacing 'Total due at signing' inline near the payment. No data-quality remediation needed.

title: Prohibited BMW ad-copy terms ('discount', 'deal') used in vehicle merchandising
quote: Dealer Discount -$10,780 ... GREAT DEAL GOOD DEAL FAIR PRICE ABOVE MARKET
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Ad Copy: Prohibited Language and Terms
recommendation: BMW-COPY-001 lists 'cheap', 'discount', 'deal', and 'affordable' among words to avoid in BMW communications. 'Dealer Discount' appears as a standard line item across the used and CPO inventory, the homepage uses 'get a great offer' and 'a price you can afford', and the third-party CarStory market widget on used VDPs renders 'GREAT DEAL / GOOD DEAL'. Brand risk is limited because these appear in used-vehicle merchandising and a third-party widget rather than BMW new-vehicle co-op creative, so this is advisory. Fix: on BMW-branded and co-op-eligible new-vehicle creative, replace 'discount/deal' framing with savings/price language BMW permits; confirm the CarStory widget wording is acceptable under the store's co-op terms or is clearly walled off as third-party content per BMW-WEB-003.
